title: the live Godot editor or running game
instructions: Host commands are gdsh commands run in the open Godot editor (the Editor Console's commands when that addon is enabled), or in a running game whose bridge is on this port: 'tree root | tree nodes --recursive', 'ls res://', and so on. Resource paths (res://...) and node paths are plain arguments Godot interprets; they are not files in this shell. 'cd'/'pwd' set and show gdsh's working directory and 'cn'/'pwn' its working node; both carry over between calls, so use absolute paths or check first. Find commands with list_commands, passing filter to search names and summaries (e.g. filter 'scene'), or 'help -s TERM' inside a script; then '<command> --help' or the help tool for subcommands and flags. Changes made through commands are real edits to the open project or game; prefer inspecting before modifying. To add a command, run 'mcp_sh_godot gdsh new NAME' in your own terminal (not this shell) and fill in the file it writes: it is listed here at once, edits apply on the next run, and one that fails to load says why when run.
setup: In each Godot project, either: with Editor Console, run 'mcp --start' in the console (or add it to its startup commands); or run 'mcp_sh_godot addon install' in the project folder (it bundles everything it needs) and enable the mcp-sh-godot plugin in Project Settings > Plugins. A game serves its own bridge on port 9511: register the mcp_sh_godot_game entry printed above. Bridge settings (port, token, commands) go in ~/.mcp-sh/godot/bridge.json or res://.mcp-sh/godot/bridge.json. Set MCP_SH_GODOT_PORT / MCP_SH_GODOT_TOKEN here if the bridge uses another port or a token.

host.hint: open the project in the Godot editor with the mcp-sh-godot plugin enabled (install it with 'mcp_sh_godot addon install')
